## What is it?
The [RDKit](https://www.rdkit.org) is a collection of cheminformatics and machine-learning software written in C++ and Python.
* [BSD license](https://github.com/rdkit/rdkit/blob/master/license.txt) - a business friendly license for open source
* Core data structures and algorithms in C++
* [Python 3.x wrapper](https://www.rdkit.org/docs/GettingStartedInPython.html) generated using Boost.Python
* Java and C# wrappers generated with SWIG
* JavaScript (generated with emscripten) and CFFI wrappers around important functionality
* 2D and 3D molecular operations
* [Descriptor](https://www.rdkit.org/docs/GettingStartedInPython.html#list-of-available-descriptors) and [Fingerprint](http://www.rdkit.org/docs/GettingStartedInPython.html#list-of-available-fingerprints) generation for machine learning
* Molecular database [cartridge](https://www.rdkit.org/docs/Cartridge.html) for PostgreSQL supporting substructure and similarity searches as well as many descriptor calculators
* Cheminformatics nodes for [KNIME](https://www.knime.com/rdkit)
* [Contrib](https://github.com/rdkit/rdkit/tree/master/Contrib) folder with useful community-contributed software harnessing the power of the RDKit
## Installation and getting started

```shell-session
$ conda install -c conda-forge rdkit
```
You can then take a look at our [Getting Started in Python](https://rdkit.org/docs/GettingStartedInPython.html) guide.

## Diagnosis

The probe aborted with an `Invar::Invariant: bad bond stereo` from `canonicalizeDoubleBond` (`source/Code/GraphMol/Canon.cpp:362`), reached via `MolToSmiles` inside tautomer enumeration.

The chain, verified with instrumented builds:
- The fixture's V3000 `CFG=1` wedge next to the sp2–sp2 N–C bond yields `STEREOATROPCW` on that single bond (with zero stereo atoms), and 2D coordinates yield a specified E/Z on the C=C bond.
- During enumeration with `removeBondStereo(false)`, an imidic-acid tautomer flips that N–C bond to a double bond; the stereo-copy sweep carries the atrop stereo onto it — an internally inconsistent double-bond stereo annotation.
- In `canonicalizeDoubleBonds`, a double bond enters the work queue only when it is `DOUBLE` with `stereo > STEREOANY` **and** ≥2 stereo atoms. But the two injected deviations broke that invariant: the neighbor-followed BFS in `getNeighboringStereoBond` lacked the stereo-atom check and queued the inconsistent bond anyway, and the filter's added `bond->setStereo(Bond::STEREONONE)` reset that same bond *after* it had been recorded as a stereo neighbor of the E/Z bond — so the BFS later handed it to `canonicalizeDoubleBond`, violating that function's PRECONDITIONs.

## Fix (2 lines in `source/Code/GraphMol/Canon.cpp`)

- `getNeighboringStereoBond` now requires `bond->getStereoAtoms().size() >= 2`, matching the queue filter, so every bond passed to `canonicalizeDoubleBond` meets its documented preconditions.
- Removed the filter's `bond->setStereo(Bond::STEREONONE)` line — it silently stripped stereo annotations from the molecule during SMILES writing and created the reset-after-queue race that triggered the abort.

## Verification

- Public reproduction from scratch (fresh configure/build/run): `workflow_completed`, exit 0.
- ~40 stereo-bearing molecules (chiral centers, E/Z, coupled/conjugated double-bond systems, ring stereo, atropisomers via CXSMILES wedges, wavy double bonds, tautomerizable heterocycles, drug-like cases) run through `canonicalize` with `removeBondStereo` both true and false: all complete, no nulls, outputs re-parse cleanly.
